doc: WHAT THIS IS
The launcher's own list of what a downloaded Girl Life archive looks like
FROM THE INSIDE. It is compiled into the binary (include_str! in
src-tauri/src/manifest.rs), so the install help works with no network at
all. The SAME file is published at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glife-launcher/GLreleases/main/pack-signatures.json
and 'Refresh pack list' fetches it on an explicit press (WP-128).
MANIFESTVERSION IS A REVISION COUNTER
Bump it by one every time this file is published with a change, or the
refresh will fetch it and correctly decide it is not newer. A fetched
copy replaces the built-in one ONLY when its number is strictly higher,
so a stale cache and a downgrade both lose. It is not a compatibility
gate: a launcher refuses a manifest it cannot honour by its FIELD NAMES
(any field not listed below is a parse failure), which also catches the
case of somebody adding a predicate and forgetting to bump the number.
WHY CONTENT AND NOT FILE NAMES
Pack names live exactly one game release ('0.9.9 Core Image Pack
(Optimized).zip', 'Bugfix Image pack 0.9.9.1.zip'), their capitalisation
drifts between uploads, and every browser appends ' (1)' to a second
download. So the name cannot decide what a file is. A zip's CENTRAL
DIRECTORY can: it is read without unpacking a single byte, it is the same
index the extractor walks, and it also catches the right-name-wrong-file
case. The file name is still read for ONE thing — the version number,
which no pack carries inside itself.
HOW MATCHING WORKS
`signatures` is ordered and the FIRST one whose every predicate holds
wins, so the specific entries must come before the general ones
(coreImages before imagePatch: the core pack is an images-only zip too,
it just also carries images/avatar.jpg). Nothing matching means the file
is not recognised — never a guess, never an unpack.
PREDICATES (all optional; a signature matches when all of its own hold)
container            'zip' | 'sevenZip' | 'qsp' — decided by the file's
MAGIC BYTES, not its extension.
topLevelIn           every file entry's first path segment must be one of
these (an entry with no directory contributes its own
file name).
requireTopLevel      each of these must appear as a first path segment.
requireEntries       these exact paths must be in the archive.
forbidEntries        these exact paths must NOT be in the archive.
requireExtension     at least one file entry must end in one of these.
minFiles / maxFiles  bounds on the number of FILE entries (directory
entries are not counted).
url                  a direct https download for this pack, or absent.
ABSENT is the normal value and the shipped one: the
packs live in a Mega folder with no anonymous direct
URL and the .qsp is posted in a forum thread behind
Cloudflare, so neither can be fetched by an HTTP GET
and neither gets a URL invented for it. Where it is
absent the launcher keeps saying where the file is
and the player fetches it themselves; where it is
present the file check and the install screen offer
a Download button. A URL arriving in a REFRESHED
manifest is network input, so the launcher fetches
it only when it points at one of its own hosts
(github.com/glife-launcher/ or
raw.githubusercontent.com/glife-launcher/) over
https — a mirror anywhere else needs a launcher
build, deliberately.
latestVersion        the newest published version OF THIS PACK, or absent
when the pack has never carried one (the hair pack).
The update check compares the packs a player has
against it. It cannot be derived from
describesGameVersion: the newest core image pack is
0.9.9 while the newest game is 0.9.9.1, so comparing
a pack against the game's version would report every
healthy install as out of date.
entriesAreArchives   the archive is a container of archives — at least
one file entry is a .zip or .7z, and every other
file entry is an archive too (.zip, .7z, .rar) or a
note (.txt, .nfo, .md), at any folder depth. This is
what a Mega bulk download looks like. One picture or
one .qsp among the entries and the predicate fails,
which is how a game-folder zip stays out of it.
ROLES (what the launcher does with a match)
coreImages   the big images/ pack — extracted first.
imagePatch   an images-only pack that is not the core one (the 'Update
X to Y' and 'Bugfix' packs are both this shape; only their
names tell them apart, and only when they have names).
coreSound    the sound/ pack.
hairColor    the optional 7z — never installed unless the user ticks it.
batch        a zip of the archives above; unpacked next to itself, then
the pieces are scanned again. Only the members that can be
packs come out of it: a .rar is NEVER unpacked (we ship no
rar reader, and mods are out of scope) and neither is
anything sorted into a folder below the packs. Both are left
inside the container, and neither is mentioned to the player
— the automatic search never talks about foreign archives.
gameFile     the .qsp itself — copied, not extracted.
UPDATING IT FOR A NEW GAME RELEASE
0. Bump manifestVersion by one — see the note above.
1. Put the release's archives in info/packs/ (gitignored).
2. cargo test dump_real_pack_shapes -- --ignored --nocapture
— it prints the container, file count, top-level segments, extensions
and marker-entry hits of every archive it finds, which is exactly the
evidence the fields below are written from.
3. Adjust only what the dump contradicts, bump `updated`,
`describesGameVersion` and every `latestVersion` the release moved,
and re-run the tests: the identification tests
replay the real archives when info/packs is present and skip when it
is not (CI has no info/).
Note what does NOT need touching: names. If the next release renames every
pack, nothing here changes.

signatures.label: Game file (.qsp)
signatures.note: A QSP container starts with the UTF-16LE bytes of 'QSPGAME\r\n' (verified against Girl Life 0.9.9.1, 91151326 bytes). The .qsp itself is obfuscated past that header, so the magic is all the evidence there is — and it is enough, because nothing else on a player's disk carries it.

signatures.label: Mega bulk download
signatures.note: Observed twice, and the two shapes are why the predicate is written the way it is. (1) 'Girl Life Image pack (1).zip', 227707218 bytes, 4 file entries at the root, every one of them a pack archive (sound zip, bugfix zip, hair 7z, update zip), zero directory entries. (2) 'Girl Life Image pack.zip', 2519605846 bytes, 10 file entries, zero directory entries, all under one folder 'Girl Life Image pack/': 7 pack zips + 'Optional Hair Color Pack.7z', plus a subfolder 'Mod Image Archive/' holding 'ibiza.7z' and 'cherrypop.rar'. WP-111: requiring EVERY entry to be a zip or a 7z made shape (2) — the whole 2.5 GB download a player actually gets — match nothing at all, so 'Install the game' reported it had found nothing (0.4.0 defect). The rar is recognised as an archive and never unpacked.

signatures.label: Core image pack
signatures.note: Observed: '0.9.9 Core Image Pack (Optimized).zip', 2033081611 bytes, 37228 file entries (directory entries are not counted), all under images/. images/avatar.jpg is shipped by the core pack and by no other pack — the same marker src/packs.rs already uses to tell a core install from a patched one. minFiles guards the case of somebody handing us a one-file zip that happens to hold avatar.jpg.

signatures.label: Sound pack
signatures.note: Observed: '0.9.9 Core Sound Pack.zip', 167698703 bytes, 139 file entries, all under sound/, every one an .mp3.

signatures.label: Optional hair color pack
signatures.note: Observed: 'Optional Hair Color Pack.7z', 12479834 bytes, 221 file entries, all under images/. It is the only 7z in the whole distribution, and its files all land under images/ — which is also why its presence cannot be seen from an installed folder (src/packs.rs check_hair_color): it only overwrites files the core pack already wrote.

signatures.label: Image update / bugfix pack
signatures.note: Observed twice: 'Update 0.9.8 to 0.9.9 Image Pack.zip' (31803722 bytes, 608 file entries) and 'Bugfix Image pack 0.9.9.1.zip' (15724182 bytes, 101 file entries). Their central directories are the same shape — an update pack and a bugfix pack cannot be told apart by content, only by their names, so the launcher treats an unnamed one as a patch to apply LAST rather than guessing which it is.
